question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =5$ and $\sigma =8.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(12.36<X<18.68) & =P(\frac{12.36-5}{8}<Z<\frac{18.68-5}{8}) \\  & =P(0.92<Z<1.71).\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/ca230d644bbf7b8e7d07c8c54816748da8dfe5dac112ccd786ab33f92733d9e8.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.92<Z<1.71) & =P(Z<1.71)-P(Z\le 0.92) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.71)-P(Z\le 0.92) \\  & =Φ(1.71)-Φ(0.92).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.71) & =0.9564 \\ Φ(0.92) & =0.8212\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.92<Z<1.71) & =Φ(1.71)-Φ(0.92) \\  & =0.9564-0.8212 \\  & =0.1352.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(12.36<X<18.68)=0.1352.
$$
